books.section: B. The Deepening of Partisanship in the Twenty-first Century
Tumultuous Years: The Trump and Biden Presidencies (2017-2022)

stem: Trump's candidacy opened fissures within the conservative movement. Which of the following best describes one of those divisions?

options.text: Populist and mainstream Republicans agreed completely on immigration and trade
options.misconception: Immigration and trade were exactly where the two wings disagreed.

options.text: Mainstream Republicans embraced Trump's calls for higher tariffs and a border wall
options.misconception: Many mainstream Republicans resisted the tariffs and the wall; they were populist positions, not establishment ones.

options.text: Trump's supporters demanded the repeal of the Second Amendment
options.misconception: Trump's supporters defended gun rights; repealing the Second Amendment was never their demand.

options.text: Mainstream Republicans grew uneasy with the populist wing's positions on immigration and trade

rationales.A: Background: immigration and trade were exactly where the two wings disagreed.
rationales.B: Background: many mainstream Republicans resisted the tariffs and the wall; they were populist positions, not establishment ones.
rationales.C: Background: Trump's supporters defended gun rights; repealing the Second Amendment was never their demand.
rationales.D: Background: divisions around immigration and trade developed as mainstream Republicans grew uneasy with the anti-establishment, populist wing.
rationales.general:
1. Picture the party splitting in two: the establishment on one side, the populists on the other.
2. Background: divisions around immigration and trade developed as mainstream Republicans grew uneasy with the populist wing.
3. Background: free trade and open immigration had been establishment conservative positions for decades — the populists challenged both.
4. The wings did not agree, the establishment did not embrace the wall, and nobody demanded repealing the Second Amendment.
Remember: the split ran along trade and immigration, populists against the establishment.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 11, 'The Election of Donald Trump (2016).' Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of an account of the 2016 election: Donald Trump focused his campaign on immigration, border security, and trade deals, and his rallies often rang with calls to build a wall along the Mexican border. His blunt style appealed to voters who felt left behind by the loss of manufacturing jobs and who disliked what they called political correctness. He won the Electoral College while losing the national popular vote.
